newsitem.title: MOROCCO: MOROCCO'S BOURSE ENDS SESSION 0.46 PCT HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: MOROCCO'S BOURSE ENDS SESSION 0.46 PCT HIGHER.

text.p: Morocco's bourse ended Monday's session 0.46 percent higher, boosted mainly by trading in largest capitalisation firms, including BCM bank, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 663.99 points from 660.97 points last Friday.
"Despite summer holidays and fluctuating trading on the market, blue-chip firms continue to attract investors' interest," a Casablanca-based broker said.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market's second largest firm with a market capitalisation of 11.8 billion dirhams, rose 14 dirhams to close at 910 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, which has diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, jumped 10 dirhams to close at 777 dirhams.
Brewery Brasseries du Maroc, a subsidiary of SNI, gained 13 dirhams to close at 2,000 dirhams.
Credit consumer firms, Magrebail and Maroc Leasing rose 32 dirhams and six dirhams to close respectively at 565 dirhams and 416 dirhams.

Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie, one of seven active banks on the bourse, was up five dirhams to 460 dirhams. BMCI's listed subsidiary credit consumer firm SOMAFIC issued 144 million dirhams ($14.4 million) medium term notes on the stock exchange.
Subscription was opened from July 10 to August 8, 1997.
SOMAFIC closed at 430 dirhams last Friday but was not traded on Monday, a stockbroker said.
Total trading volume more than doubled to 144.8 million dirhams from 64 million dirhams on Friday.
Exchanges on the official market were slightly down to 21.3 million dirhams from 23.6 million over the previous session.
